title: Void Ending in a Trine to Neptune
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Neptune, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his drifting mist. Neptune is unknown to Picatrix; the planet was found in 1846, by calculation before anyone saw it, and the source never mentions it. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of the lunar doctrine, not the doctrine itself. Named for the Greek lord of the sea, it is read as cold, blue, and dissolving: a course that closes on it ends in something misty, where edges soften and matters drift rather than conclude.
